anomalies.observed: R70 (19k6) runs from the 5 V output node (the L2 output / C5 top) to the NET0069 junction. NET0069 is the same node as REG3 FB (pin 24) and the R67/R49 junction. R67 (6k8) also runs from +5V to that node, so R70 sits in parallel with the top feedback resistor, giving an effective top resistance of about 5.05k.
anomalies.expected: With only R67 (6k8) as the top divider resistor and R49 (1k3) as the bottom, Vout = 0.8*(1+6.8/1.3) ≈ 4.98 V, matching the 5 V rail. The parallel 19k6 would pull the output to about 3.9 V. The spec gives the 5 V rail and the formula Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6) without listing R70 as a component.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (1/6): R70 19k6 between +5V and NET0069; R67 6k8 and R49 1k3 form the divider labelled "Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)"
A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V.

anomalies.impact: If R70 is really in parallel with the feedback top resistor, the 5 V rail would regulate to roughly 3.9 V instead of 5 V. That would undervolt the servo and 5 V distribution and the LD39200 input, and could make the 3.3 V LDO drop out. Lower confidence because R70 may be an original, intentional element that the author did not document.

parsed.summary: Most of the power, sensing and peripheral wiring checks out, but the 5 V feedback network appears to have an extra 19k6 resistor (R70) in parallel with the top feedback resistor, which would shift the regulated output well below the intended 5 V. Confidence is moderate because the drawing layout is ambiguous.
